en.bestFor: Turning an idea, article or set of notes into a clear concept explainer for Reels, Shorts, marketing or presentations — any topic that is clearer as an explanation graph than as a character holding props.
en.structure: Each clip runs 3–8 seconds and the count follows the content: about 1–2 clips for a micro short, 2–4 for 15–20s, 4–6 for 30–45s, and 7–10 for a full 50–60s explainer.
en.hook: The first one to two seconds stack at least two hooks at once — a punchy spoken line plus a visual or sound opener, such as the character sliding into frame, an oversized prop popping up, or a sudden whoosh.
en.arc: Picks the pattern that suits the source, e.g. surprise → setup → how it works → consequence → takeaway for education, or pain point → reveal → proof → call to action for products. The main answer is held back until near the end, and the video finishes on a clean resting payoff rather than looping.
en.narrator: A warm adult male voice narrates every line from off-screen, in the third person. The character stays silent and never lip-syncs. With a character on screen, each clip is a new performance: sometimes stage left, sometimes stage right; they may run, jump, point, pull or push a drawn object, and turn their head left or right. Do not repeat the same move. The narrator may call them by name.
en.visual: A fixed whiteboard-doodle look: bold, slightly wobbly black lines with flat marker fills on a white canvas. Every topic is an explanation graph — comparison, before/after, cause and effect, steps, labeled parts, flow, or a chart — plus extra objects and doodles that explain the idea. With a character on screen, each clip offers a fresh idea: a different side of the frame, a new action such as run, jump, point, pull, or push, and a head turn left or right. Short beat titles and diagram labels sit on the canvas.
en.audio: Background music follows the emotional turn of the script, with quick sound effects (pops, whooshes, dings) timed to visual changes. Narration is voice only; beat titles and diagram labels may sit on the canvas.
en.rules: You must pick an aspect ratio. The source's meaning is kept and no facts are invented. The explanation graph is the spine of every topic. With a character on screen, clips must not repeat: vary left and right staging, actions (run, jump, point, pull, push), and which way the head turns, and give each clip a fresh visual idea. Beat titles and diagram labels are allowed. The whiteboard style and character design stay locked. You approve the storyboard before any video is made.
